passage: I'm Jyoti, and I still think about that Ganesh visarjan night with Rehana. The street was packed, drums going, strangers hugging and jumping with their arms in the air. Rehana grabbed my hands and we spun, laughing till our faces hurt. It felt like everybody was one happy body. Then the mood shifted. Somebody near the back started shoving to get closer to the truck, and the shoulders around us stopped swaying and turned hard. I saw Rehana's smile go tight. We had already agreed on the lane by the pharmacy as our way out, so we slipped along the edge and stood there catching our breath. I was sad to leave, but glad we had a plan.

qa.q: Which lane had Jyoti and Rehana agreed on as their way out?
qa.a: They had agreed on the lane by the pharmacy.

qa.q: What did Jyoti feel when the crowd's mood shifted?
qa.a: Jyoti felt uneasy and tense, seeing the shoulders turn hard and Rehana's smile go tight. Jyoti was also sad to leave, so the feelings were mixed.

qa.q: What was wise about how Jyoti and Rehana handled the crowd?
qa.a: They noticed the mood change early and used the exit they had agreed on, rather than staying to see if it calmed.

qa.q: How might Rehana have felt when the pushing began?
qa.a: Rehana's smile going tight suggests worry, though Rehana may also have been reluctant to end the fun, so leaving quietly respected both feelings.

grounding: A young adult reads jumping, hugging and dancing at a festival as shared joy, then notices the crowd shift and uses an exit plan.

passage: Coach's note, Saturday, district football final. From my seat by the pitch I saw the crowd behind the goal cheering hard when Chaitanya scored: jumping, arms round each other, a few people dancing on the steps. That was ordinary joy. Chaitanya, still in the stands after being subbed, was clapping and hugging a teammate. Later, when we equalised late, the noise changed. People started pushing along the rail. Chaitanya glanced at the staircase, tapped the teammate's arm and the two of them moved to the side exit. I didn't tell them to. I'm Pradeep, the coach, and next week I'll go over exit points with the whole squad, so leaving early is normal.

qa.q: Where did Chaitanya go when the noise changed?
qa.a: Chaitanya and a teammate moved to the side exit.

qa.q: What was Chaitanya likely feeling when glancing at the staircase?
qa.a: Chaitanya was probably uneasy about the pushing along the rail, and chose safety over staying for the celebration. A different reading is that Chaitanya just wanted to beat the rush, since the note cannot say.

qa.q: What could Pradeep do so players know how to handle a crowd?
qa.a: Go over exit points with the whole squad and make it normal to leave early when the mood shifts.

qa.q: How might the teammate have felt about leaving?
qa.a: The teammate may have wanted to stay for the celebration, but followed after Chaitanya's tap, which suggests trust.

grounding: A coach sees crowd joy at a match turn into unsafe pushing and a player moves to an exit.

passage:
Sunday night, hostel.
What a match. When the last ball went for four, the whole East Stand jumped at once. Strangers hugged me. Pranav lifted me off my feet, screaming. I've never felt joy like that in a crowd, like one big body.
Then it changed, fast. At the exit ramp people kept surging forward, still singing, but the singing turned into shoving. My arms got pinned. A man behind us yelled "Push!" and nobody could. I saw Pranav's face go pale. Remembering the side gate we had noticed on the way in, I grabbed his sleeve and we edged sideways along the wall till we got out.
We stood on the road shaking and laughing at the same time. Next match: we pick the exit before the first ball, and we leave five minutes early if the ramp looks packed.
— Mridul

qa.q: Which gate did Mridul and Pranav use to get out?
qa.a: The side gate they had noticed on the way in.

qa.q: What was Mridul feeling when the whole stand jumped at the last ball?
qa.a: Mridul felt pure joy, like the crowd was one big body; later that joy turned into fear when the shoving started at the exit.

qa.q: Which choice kept Mridul and Pranav safe, and what is their plan now?
qa.a: Edging sideways along the wall to the side gate got them out; next time they will pick the exit early and leave before the ramp packs.

qa.q: What was it like for Pranav when the crowd began shoving?
qa.a: His face went pale, suggesting he was frightened once the singing crowd became a crush.

grounding: Shows a young adult reading crowd hugging and jumping as shared joy, then noticing the shift to unsafe pushing and using an exit plan.

passage:

Mahima: near the dhak drummers. everyone's dancing, it's so good
Disha: I see you! you're jumping like a kid 😄

Disha: I can see it too. the crowd's moving in waves, not dancing any more
Mahima: I can't really turn around
Disha: go left with the flow towards the food stalls. don't fight it
Mahima: ok moving
Disha: I'm at the tea stall by the blue tent. that's our spot if we lose each other
Mahima: made it. my dupatta got pulled, my heart is racing
Disha: breathe. we're staying at the edge now
Mahima: yes. and we told the volunteer at the gate it's too packed, they're closing it for a bit

qa.a: The tea stall by the blue tent.

qa.q: How can you tell Mahima's mood changed during the evening?
qa.a: At first Mahima is happy dancing near the drummers, but once the pushing starts Mahima writes about a racing heart, which shows fear; some of the racing may also be from the dancing.

qa.q: What did Disha and Mahima do well once the crowd turned pushy?
qa.a: Disha told Mahima to move with the flow to the side, they agreed a meeting spot, stayed at the edge and told a volunteer, who closed the gate for a while.

passage: The kabaddi final at the Mandvi village fair ended with the home team winning by one point. The crowd poured onto the dusty ground, dancing to the dhol, lifting the players up. Pooja and Sonali danced too, arms in the air. Then Pooja noticed the rope around the ground sagging as more people pressed in from the road side. A small boy near the rope was crying, squeezed between two men. The drumming went on, but the shouts now sounded different, sharper. "Sonali, we're going to the temple steps," Pooja said, taking her friend's hand. On the way she lifted the crying boy up to a man from his village, who carried him out. From the temple steps, higher up, they watched the crowd thin slowly. Sonali was still grinning. "You spoil every party," she teased. Pooja just pointed at the fallen rope.

qa.q: What did the crowd do after the kabaddi final ended?
qa.a: The crowd poured onto the dusty ground, dancing to the dhol and lifting the players up.

qa.q: What made Pooja uneasy even while the celebration went on?
qa.a: She grew uneasy and alert when she saw the rope sagging, a small boy crying and the shouts turning sharper; Sonali, still grinning, felt only the joy.

qa.q: What small steps did Pooja take when the crowd shifted?
qa.a: She moved Sonali to the higher temple steps and handed the crying boy to a man from his village so he could be carried out.

qa.q: How did Sonali see Pooja's decision to leave?
qa.a: Sonali teased that Pooja spoils every party, as she was still enjoying the celebration and had not noticed the danger.

grounding: Shows a young adult reading a celebrating crowd and noticing when it shifts toward unsafe pressing, then moving to safety.

passage: When the late goal went in at the Osaka stadium, the away end exploded. Kaito grabbed Tariq and they bounced together, strangers hugging them, scarves whirling, someone's drink raining down. Tariq laughed until his ribs hurt. It was pure joy, and he could see it in every face around him. Then, down near the stairs, the bouncing changed. People at the front had stopped jumping, but those behind hadn't. A woman was pressed against the railing, her smile gone, arms folded up to protect her chest. Someone shouted, "Stop pushing!" Tariq tugged Kaito's sleeve. "Look at the front. That's not dancing anymore." Before kick-off they had noticed a side exit by gate 14. They edged sideways along the row, out of the flow, and waved to a steward, pointing at the railing. The steward radioed, and within a minute the crowd behind was being slowed.

qa.q: Where had Tariq and Kaito noticed a side exit?
qa.a: By gate 14.

qa.q: What was Tariq feeling when he saw the woman pressed against the railing?
qa.a: Tariq felt alarmed; the faces at the front showed fear rather than joy, so he read that the celebration had turned into unsafe pushing.

qa.q: Which steps kept them and others safer?
qa.a: Noting an exit before kick-off, moving sideways out of the flow, and alerting a steward to the crush at the railing.

qa.q: What was it like for the woman at the railing while the bouncing continued behind her?
qa.a: She was likely frightened and struggling to breathe freely, arms up to protect herself, while people behind still thought it was only celebration.

grounding: It illustrates a young adult reading crowd jumping and hugging as shared joy, then noticing the shift to unsafe pushing and using an exit plan and a steward.
